cards.explanation: The answer is beasts and cattle. “Their idols weigh down beasts and cattle.” (Isaiah 46:1) Bel and Nebo are gods, and here their idols are cargo. Somebody's poor animal is doing the hauling for a god. I've been carried around a kitchen in a box, but at least nobody expected me to answer prayers on the way.

The answer is False. The text says the gods “…cower; they crouch together, unable to relieve the burden…” (Isaiah 46:2) A god who can't lift his own load is in a rough spot. That's a lot of crouching for something people are supposed to depend on.

The answer is that they go into captivity. The gods “…themselves go into captivity.” (Isaiah 46:2) They can't relieve the burden, and they can't escape being carried off either. Think about that for a second, friends. The ones people were supposed to lean on get taken away.

The answer is that He carried them along. The LORD says they've been “…sustained from the womb, carried along since birth.” (Isaiah 46:3) Look at the contrast with the verses before. The idols have to be carried, and here the LORD is the One doing the carrying. That's a very different kind of god.

The answer is that He will bear them up. The LORD says, “…I will bear you up when you turn gray.” (Isaiah 46:4) The same LORD who carried them from birth keeps carrying them when their hair turns gray. Nobody gets set down halfway. If you've ever worried about getting older, friends, read that verse twice.

The answer is “made.” The LORD says, “I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you.” (Isaiah 46:4) He says He made them, and He says He will carry them. Compare that to the idols, which a goldsmith fashioned and people lift to their shoulders. (Isaiah 46:6; 46:7) The LORD carries His people, and the people carry the idol.

The answer is a god. The people “…hire a goldsmith to fashion it into a god, so they can bow down and worship.” (Isaiah 46:6) Think about the order of that, friends. The people pay a worker to make the thing, and then they bow to it. They're worshiping something that was handed to them by a paid craftsman.

The answer is that it stands without budging. The text says, “…they set it in its place, and there it stands, not budging from that spot.” (Isaiah 46:7) It stays right where they put it. The people lift it to their shoulder and carry it along first, and then it stands there. I think a god who can't budge is a hard one to ask for rescue.

The answer is True. “They cry out to it, but it does not answer; it saves no one from his troubles.” (Isaiah 46:7) People call out, and nothing comes back. Picture shouting into a room and hearing only your own echo. That's the god they paid so much to make.

The answer is False. The LORD says there are no other gods like Him. He says, “…I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me.” (Isaiah 46:9) Notice He says it twice. When He tells them to remember what happened long ago, this is what He wants them to remember.

The answer is “stand.” The LORD says, “I say, ‘My purpose will stand, and all My good pleasure I will accomplish.’” (Isaiah 46:10) Whatever He purposes holds. Compare that with the gods who crouched and went off into captivity. His purpose stays standing.

The answer is a bird of prey. The LORD says, “I summon a bird of prey from the east, a man for My purpose from a far-off land.” (Isaiah 46:11) The bird is the picture the LORD uses. The one it stands for is a man, called from a far-off land for the LORD's purpose.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Truly I have spoken, and truly I will bring it to pass. I have planned it, and I will surely do it.” (Isaiah 46:11) That's a lot of certainty packed into two sentences. He says “truly” twice in that one verse. He says it, plans it, and does it.

The answer is that He is bringing it near. The LORD says, “I am bringing My righteousness near; it is not far away…” (Isaiah 46:13) He just called them stubborn and far removed from righteousness, and then He brings it close. He's the One closing the distance, friends. And in the same verse He says He will grant salvation to Zion.

The answer is that it will not be delayed. The LORD says, “…My salvation will not be delayed.” (Isaiah 46:13) That's what He says about when it will come. I've been left waiting in a dark drawer, so I know what a promise like that means.
